newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE cocoa races higher after NY-led short-covering.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE cocoa races higher after NY-led short-covering.

text.p: A burst of New York-inspired short-covering pulled London cocoa futures out of their gloom as benchmark prices ended at their highest levels in more than a week.
But traders stressed the downtrend which dragged prices to a sequence of 18-month lows did not seem to be exhausted.

Prices raced through initial resistance in the afternoon, carrying the key March position from a contract low of 861 in the morning to an impressive finish of 885 stg a tonne, the highest since January 16 and up 23 stg on the day.
The second-month May zoomed past buy stops at 900 to stand 24 stg up at the close at 910 -- the highest since January 7.
"There was a lot of trade on both sides of the market. People were liquidating longs, others were aggressively covering shorts and there was definitely some industry buying," said one trader.
Others said oversold technicals in New York meant the market couldn't sustain the downside and needed a correction. A slight drop in the dollar against European currencies also underpinned New York.
The session saw extensive buying from locals following bids by Phibro, traders said.
But despite the encouraging close, traders saw no reason to overhaul what they see as a fundamentally bleak outlook for cocoa with abundant supplies.
"I still see no reason to suggest that the downside is finished," said one trader. "The market will pull back again."
Friday's turnover totalled 7,392 lots including 1,000 lots crossed on May 89 stg. Switches saw March/May to trade into 22 from 25.
March needs to breach 890 and 900 to trigger follow-up orders. Support is Friday's low of 861 which is the lowest from 18-months on second mont 44-171-542 8072
